rationale: Corrected a retained claim against its source: the prepare-recovery rejection path (handlePrepareReply) contains no repair at all, while the IsLeader-gated makeBallot-plus-prepare restarts belong to the proposal-phase handlers. The behavior entry is revised under its existing id with the affected interpretation named, and the recovery-authority account is updated to cite the correct sites; the conclusion is unchanged and in fact rests on a simpler basis.

knowledge.statement: In handlePrepareReply a reply whose Ballot differs from lb.lastTriedBallot increments lb.nacks and returns before the reply is appended to lb.prepareReplies, and no repair is attempted on that path; the sub-case dispatch is guarded by len(lb.prepareReplies) >= SlowQuorumSize(), so a recovery whose answers are all rejections keeps only its own self reply, selects no sub-case and emits no PreAccept, Accept or Commit for that attempt. The makeBallot-plus-prepare restarts that do exist live in the two proposal-phase handlers (handlePreAcceptReply and handleAcceptReply) when a majority of replies reports a higher ballot, and each of those is executed only while r.IsLeader is true.
knowledge.conditions: Recovery where the replicas that answer the Prepare have a stored bal above the recovering replica's fixed tried ballot, so every answer is a rejection rather than a matching-ballot reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1222, with epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451, 855-868 and 1016-1033).
knowledge.changed_premise: Corrected where the IsLeader-gated repair lives: the prepare-recovery rejection path contains no repair at all (it only counts nacks and returns), while the makeBallot-plus-bcastPrepare restarts are in handlePreAcceptReply and handleAcceptReply. The conclusion (a fully rejected recovery attempt stays inert with no enabled repair for a non-designated replica) is unchanged; the earlier wording attributed the gated repair to handlePrepareReply.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: recovery authority in the captured EPaxos package is bounded by the recovering replica's fixed ballot, and the boundary is measured with declared comparisons for both the instance owner and a non-owner. Owner case (receipt 911d45335b3047178a6fd739f24b2cfb, fixed experiment adfa9c6d31ca481896e5ca1277f6cdf4-experiment): two attempts at ballot 0 against peers storing 7 append only the self reply, dispatch nothing and emit no follow-up (comparisons 0 and 1 violated, witnesses 20 and 25), while the same call after the target's own BeTheLeader uses ballot 10, matches the peers and completes the instance (control comparisons 2 and 3 hold, evaluated 31 and 32). Non-owner boundary (receipt c342db60ffff4e42889bf53646049491, corrected successor of 43b9bbefd939404e9ad77b1e71564e2d-experiment, 23 parsed events, now without diagnostics): with the same premise of peers storing ballot 7, the attempt by replica 1 whose fixed ballot is 6 produces no matching reply, dispatches nothing and emits no follow-up (comparison 0 violated, witness 12), whereas the attempt by replica 3 whose fixed ballot is 8 is joined by the peers, matches two replies and dispatches its phase-1 proposal (comparison 1 holds, evaluated 17) - so the gate bites exactly when the recoverer's fixed ballot is below the stored one. The superseded boundary receipt c68b6de1442e45ffa00ddaf4df9b32e6 carries the same events; its comparisons came back violated/unknown only because both round-start prerequisite aliases had been left unpinned to their rounds, an observation-construction defect corrected in the successor. No repair exists inside the snapshot for the blocked case, and the prepare-recovery path has none of its own: handlePrepareReply counts the rejection and returns (epaxos/epaxos.go:1216-1219), the makeBallot-plus-prepare restarts that do exist sit in the proposal-phase handlers and are gated on r.IsLeader (epaxos/epaxos.go:855-868 and 1016-1033), and makeBallot's climb above maxRecvBallot is likewise gated on it (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451); the blocked replica's attempts therefore stay inert until the master designates it through BeTheLeader (epaxos/epaxos.go:1121-1125).

knowledge.assertion: the prepare-recovery rejection has no repair; the gated restarts are on the proposal-phase handlers
fixed ballot per replica, climbing only with IsLeader; boundary against the peers' stored ballot

counterevidence: The gate is a boundary, not a blanket inability: the owner control and the above-ballot round both show the same instance advancing when the recoverer's ballot exceeds the stored one, so replicas whose fixed ballot is above the stored ballot are unaffected.
The peers' answers are legitimate protocol behaviour: each reports the ballot it stored, and the rejected tries were genuinely below it, so the rejections do not themselves violate a peer duty.

The blocked state requires a stored ballot above the recoverer's fixed ballot; in the receipts it came from a recovery attempt that failed after broadcasting its Prepare, which is a permitted failure but a specific one.

The recoverers that hold the instance without its command cannot substitute another path: their only entry point is startRecoveryForInstance, whose prepare uses makeBallot's fixed ballot; a replica that already holds the value is not blocked in the same way, as the value-adoption control showed.

The conclusion does not depend on where the gated restarts sit: the prepare-recovery path has no repair (epaxos/epaxos.go:1216-1219), and the two restarts that exist belong to the proposal-phase handlers, which a blocked recoverer never reaches because its prepare never completes.
limitations: One configuration (N=5, F=2, instance (0,0)) with the stored ballot fixed at 7; the boundary was exercised at fixed ballots 0, 6 and 8, so an intermediate stored ballot and higher ballot rounds (id+2N and beyond) were not exercised.

The harness invoked startRecoveryForInstance directly instead of waiting for the executor's COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417) and scheduled all deliveries explicitly, so the retry cadence and transport timing are modelled.

The premise that the accepting peers store the higher ballot was produced by failing replica 2 after its Prepare broadcast; a real deployment could reach the same state through the same permitted failure, which was not exercised end-to-end.

No client or executor existed in these runs, so the blocked replica's consequence for a waiting client is characterised at the protocol level (an uncommitted instance whose dependents cannot execute) rather than measured as a completion interval.
interpretations.joint_history: Indices 0-6, 10, 11, 15-17, 20, 21, 23-28 and 31-35 belong to receipt 911d45335b3047178a6fd739f24b2cfb (owner-recoverer run); indices 8, 12, 14, 17, 19 and 20 belong to receipt c342db60ffff4e42889bf53646049491 (non-owner boundary run, same instance (0,0) and same scenario, corrected alias successor). Each statement names its receipt; no measurement is combined across executions.
